messages:
Maria Chen: quick sync — thinking about a 'slim translation proxy' pattern. Gateway only does auth, routing, rate-limit; no field-level proto translation. clients talk protobuf over gRPC or REST*json, we standardize on ptypes and server adapters that accept both. Pros: simpler gateway, less CPU, better telemetry mapping. Cons: clients must carry translation logic. Thoughts? :thinking:
Kevin Patel: I like the idea of keeping gateway dumb. Two questions: 1) how do we guarantee stable contracts for clients? 2) what about browser clients that can't speak gRPC?
Olivia Gomez: For (2) we can offer a small client shim (wasm) that does proto<->json conversion in-edge/browser. Or fallback REST endpoints for public clients. But that adds maintenance.
Samir Rao: Telemetry concern: if gateway doesn't transcode, we lose structured field-level signals for usage-based metrics and routing via model-version headers. We could ask backends to emit standardized telemetry events. Need an invariant: request metadata must include canonical field paths used for routing/quota.
Jamie Liu: +1 to Samir. Also quota enforcement: current quota keys read from decoded proto fields (e.g., tenant_id, feature_toggle). If gateway strips translation, how will rate-limiters access tenant_id? We could require an X-Redwood-Tenant header upstream.
Maria Chen: proposal: require canonical headers (X-RW-tenant, X-RW-feature) for all requests at gateway. Client shims populate them. Gateway enforces quota on headers. Backends still get full proto payload. That keeps gateway simple while preserving quotas/telemetry.
Kevin Patel: Sounds workable. Edge case: third-party integrators that can't change clients. Do we plan a backend-side adapter to accept loosely-structured JSON and populate headers? That's back to gateway-ish behavior.
Olivia Gomez: Implementation sketch:
```
# envoy filter pseudo
- match: /v1/infer
  require_headers: [X-RW-tenant]
  route: backend-infer
  rate_limit: { key: header:X-RW-tenant }
```
Client shim would call gRPC directly or POST JSON to /public/v1/infer which maps to same backend.
```
POST /public/v1/infer
body: {input: "...", tenant: "acme"}
```

Samir Rao: For telemetry: backend emits span attributes: rw.tenant, rw.model.variant, rw.request.type. We bind those to our metrics pipeline. That avoids gateway having to decode proto fields.
Jamie Liu: Rollout UX: canary for the shim requirement — enable header enforcement only for 10% and log rejected. Dashboard shows missing-header count + client ids. If trend down, ramp enforcement.
Maria Chen: OK next steps: (1) add header contract to API docs + client shim template (2) prototype envoy require_headers rule and logging (3) add backend span attributes checklist. I'll file RFC after prototyping. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Deploy Bot: new-deploy: envoy-proto-rule-spike merged to staging by @olivia
Olivia Gomez: Deploy note: staging shows ~3% increase in latency when shimming via wasm in browser; gRPC path unchanged. Will detail in RFC.
